item.title: A database with refined plant functional type attribution at eddy covariance sites for enhanced land surface model simulations
item.description:
A database with refined plant functional type attribution at eddy covariance sites for enhanced land surface model simulations
Vincent Tartaglione, Fabienne Maignan, Vladislav Bastrikov, Philippe Peylin, and Cédric Bacour
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-796,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Flux tower measurements are widely used for evaluation and calibration of land surface models. However, the vegetation information surrounding the towers is usually given in a form not directly usable by models. We combined multiple information sources to describe the vegetation surrounding 229 flux tower sites from major networks, in terms of fractions of plant functional types. For each site, we provide three flags that aim to help modelers select the most relevant sites for their study.

item.title: High spatial resolution emissions inventory (2005–2022) in Chile from livestock and waste sectors
item.description:
High spatial resolution emissions inventory (2005–2022) in Chile from livestock and waste sectors
Diana Rojas, Nicolas Alamos, Nicolas Huneeus, Mariel Opazo, Ignacio Leiva, Kevin Basoa, Ignacio Beltran, Tia Scarpelli, Mauricio Osses, and Juan Pablo Boisier
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-850,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas, but Chile reported its livestock and waste emissions only by region. We mapped these emissions, plus nitrous oxide, ammonia and other volatile gases, at about one-kilometre resolution for 2005 to 2022 using national statistics and site records. Methane rose by about a third, driven mainly by landfills. A few large landfills dominate, while livestock emissions spread across southern pastures. The open dataset supports air-quality modelling and climate policy.
